summary: Bitterroot National Forest L-4 tower (1931) on Bald Top Mountain with 1943 personnel; sources agree on 1965 but differ on whether it was destroyed or removed.

facts.status_note: Both sources date the end to 1965; one says destroyed, the other says removed

events.note: Daily Missoulian report, May 8, 1930, as quoted by Kemnow: Darby district program includes a lookout on Baldtop mountain (a plan, not a completion)
Known lookout personnel: Mr. and Mrs. Steve Thatcher
firelookout.com says destroyed; Kemnow's page lists 'Removed' under 1965

evidence.quote: Known lookout personnel: 1943: Mr. and Mrs. Steve Thatcher.

evidence.supports: Location 14 miles southeast of Hamilton, Ravalli County
Daily Missoulian 1930 report of a planned lookout
evidence.quote: Plans are made to build a lookout on Baldtop mountain.

evidence.supports: Forest Service Darby district program for the 1930 season
evidence.quote: Employes of the Forest Service in the Darby district with District Ranger C. W. Shockley are launching an extensive program for the 1930 season.

evidence.supports: Kemnow lists the tower as removed in 1965
FFLA Montana list: Bald Top Mountain, Ravalli, tower, gone
evidence.quote: Bald Top Mountain Ravalli 46.09560 -113.93547 Tower Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says the tower was destroyed in 1965; Kemnow's page lists it as removed in 1965. Both give the same year but a different end, so the story reports both and does not choose.

sources.title: Bald Top Mtn. Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: The 1930 Daily Missoulian item is a plan, so it is an 'other' event; the 1931 built date rests on firelookout.com alone. The destroyed-or-removed disagreement is recorded as a resolved conflict, not corrected. Elevation 7,355 ft per firelookout.com is now recorded as elevation_ft and evidenced; a WebSearch snippet giving 7,313 ft for the peak was not read and is not used. No source describes the summit today. Record kind 'tower' and status 'gone' are consistent with the sources, so no correction is proposed.
